title: Charles VI to Count Leopold Viktorin Windischgrätz, Vienna, 3 February 1720 (DECODE R5019/R5020), Chancellery key R5017

steps.what: Fetched DECODE R5017-R5024 images and record pages; the letter records point to keys R5017 and R5018.
Mírka 2012 found: describes the private key and the Reichshofrat nomenclator, prints no decryption; web search found none.
Transcribed R5017 in full (syllabary 1-400, nomenclator 401-999; 41 low-confidence cells flagged).
No. 1 cipher numbers (26 passages) from the register copy, checked against the autograph (ct_1720-02-03.txt).
No. 1 decoded with R5017 via dec.py; key slips 31 = zu and 268 = ein found from sense; 446 and 638 stay uncertain.
All 35 passages read as German fitting the clear context and the 1720-22 diplomacy (Alberoni's fall, Beretti Landi marriage proposal).

Entry split under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): Nos. 2, 3, 6 in the private key R5018 moved to windischgraetz1720b with key5018.md and dec_R5018_letters.md; this entry keeps No. 1 in the Chancellery key R5017. Fraction recomputed on No. 1: 221/223.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): No. 1 linked to its number runs (ct_1720-02-03.txt), the clear-text transcription and the decryption dec_R5017_letter.md; key_file the R5017 syllabary and nomenclator transcriptions

Verification 5 (plain bar, 23 Oct 2026): German (explicit-hole bar): the 26 passages in their clear context plain 0.923, explicit 0.962. Rescored with research/reading_audit/v2_score.py; all entries keep read; reading_review notes record both scores.

Read share recounted over cipher words only (README Conventions, 16 Nov 2026) on No1_reading.md: the 27 ⟦ ⟧ spans (the 26 cipher passages of dec_R5017_letter.md) counted, the clear text of clear_1720-02-03.txt left out; holes by words with the v2_score rules (apostrophe words as one). 133 cipher words, 6 holes ([zu] x3 for cell 31, [?ein]ichn for 268, [446], [638]). 0.985 (whole letter) -> 0.955; stays read, class unchanged. fraction_read (221 of 223 groups) unchanged.

outcome.method_basis: The DECODE letter records point to the Chancellery key R5017, which Mirka (2012) had described; the project transcribed it and applied it directly to No. 1, with two key slips corrected.
outcome.fraction_read_source: dec_R5017_letter.md: 223 cipher tokens of No. 1; the uncertain nomenclator values 446 and 638 counted unread (221/223).
outcome.notes: The key survives and was applied directly; no cryptanalysis. Split on 14 Oct 2026: the letters in the Emperor's private key R5018 (Nos. 2, 3, 6) are windischgraetz1720b.

texts.label: No. 1, Vienna, 3 Feb 1720 (R5019 autograph, R5020 copy)
texts.summary: Charles VI to his envoy at The Hague, Count Windischgrätz: report everything to Pentenriedter, confide in Cadogan; with Alberoni expelled from Spain, France may seek a separate peace with 'the Duc d'Anjou' (Philip V) through Morville; bring the King of Portugal into the Alliance; giving Sardinia to the Duke of Lorraine is 'sehr ideal'; the Emperor insists on the equivalent for Montferrat.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (plain bar, VERIFY5_BRIEF): German, not French: explicit-hole bar. The 26 cipher passages of dec_R5017_letter.md, each with the clear words before it (research/reading_audit/v5b_wtable.py): plain 0.923 (24/26), explicit 0.962. Keeps read.

texts.note: 16 Nov 2026: read share over cipher words only 0.955: 127 of the 133 words in the 27 ⟦ ⟧ spans of No1_reading.md read (the 26 passages A-Z, one split in two). Holes: the three [zu] (key cell 31 reads 'el', the sense needs zu), [?ein]ichn (cell 268 'em'), and the numbers [446] and [638], one word each. The surviving key's own values that give no sense have no one-digit correction, so they stay holes (README Conventions, 14 Nov 2026). The clear text of the register copy around the spans is left out. Whole letter, clear included, not the measure: 0.985, the figure recorded before. With the key cell 31 accepted as zu, 130 of 133 (0.977).
